newsitem.title: FRANCE: Total and Saga in new oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Total and Saga in new oil deal.

text.p: French oil company Total SA said on Monday it had struck a new alliance with Norway's Saga Petroleum to widen their oil exploration activities in the North Sea.

The two companies, which already cooperate in an area west of the Shetland Islands, will search for oil in deep waters on the Atlantic Margins, stretching from the Shetlands to the west of Ireland, Total said in a statement.
The two firms "will share their experience, resources and expertise in deep-sea exploration and production," Total said.
"The alliance also supports Total's strategy of renewing its reserves in the North Sea, particularly through deep-sea operations in regions that have recently been opened to exploration," it said.
It gave no financial information about the deal.
Total said it already operates in several exploration blocks west of the Shetlands and drilled two wells in 1995 and 1996 in water depths of some 600 metres.
It said it would also start drilling next spring on a permit in the Porcupine Basin west of Ireland. Water depths there range between 600 and 1,000 metres.
